To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

we have designed, modeled, fabricated, and characterized Ge-on-Si Single Photon Avalanche Diodes (SPAD) that show promise to be competitive with other SPAD detectors at 1310 and even 1550 nm, and that are fully integrated on a Si platform.
Ge-on-Si avalanche photodiodes have a low noise-equivalent power, low jitter, and low after-pulsing at both 1310 nm and 1550nm.
Ge-on-Si avalanche photodiodes are promising candidates for single-photon detection in the near-infrared region.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the design, modeling, and fabrication of Ge-on-Si avalanche diodes for single-photon counting applications.
the development and characterization of Ge-on-Si photonic integrated circuits for use in single-photon counting applications.
the development of single-photon detectors based on the Ge-on-Si technology.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
Ge-on-Si SPADs have been demonstrated to be an excellent technology for the realization of high-performance single-photon avalanche detectors for a wide range of applications.
the Ge-on-Si technology is a very promising technology for single photon detection.
the Ge-on-Si SPAD detectors have the potential to be the best SPAD detectors available, with the best performance in terms of detection efficiency, dark count rate, afterpulsing, and jitter.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the epitaxial growth of Ge-on-Si is an attractive approach for the realization of single-photon detectors with a large number of applications in quantum optics, optical communications, and quantum information.

we have developed the first Ge-on-Si SPAD detectors, with performance at 1310 and now at 1550 nm that is comparable to that of commercial SPAD devices, but with the potential to integrate with Si CMOS electronics.

we demonstrated the first Ge-on-Si SPADs that are fully compatible with the Si CMOS technology, and that they are suitable for applications at 1310 and even 1550 nm, with a potential for low noise, high efficiency, and high timing resolution.
